item: The mkdir lock records the pid of the shell holding it where bash has no BASHPID (macOS bash 3.2) and a takeover puts back a live launcher's lock
summary: On a bash without BASHPID the owner token was the launcher's own $$ in every subshell, so the deferred child holding the lock was recorded as its parent and a second launcher took the lock over once the parent exited. The token is now the holder's own pid (BASHPID, else the PPID of a one-line sh forked by the holding shell itself). The takeover reads what it moved and puts a lock back whose owner is not the one judged dead and is alive (the read-to-mv race), leaving a window of two commands instead of the gap between reading and moving. Both are red without the change and tested here on Linux by unsetting BASHPID and by forcing the interleaving with a mv wrapper; never run on a real macOS. Stated limit: the Windows wrapper's named mutex has no Global prefix (per-session; launchers in different sessions do not exclude each other) and was left alone because it cannot be run here.
